entities.summary:
The 1983 Beirut barracks bombing was a devastating suicide bombing that took place on October 23, 1983, in Beirut, Lebanon. This attack, carried out by Islamic Jihad Organization, targeted the French and US military barracks, killing 299 people and injuring over 100. The bombing was a significant event in the history of the Lebanese Civil War and had far-reaching consequences for the region.

The bombing was carried out by a group of terrorists who infiltrated the US military barracks and detonated a truck bomb, causing widespread destruction and loss of life. The attack was a major blow to the US and French military presence in Lebanon and marked a turning point in the conflict.

The legacy of the 1983 Beirut barracks bombing can be seen in the ongoing tensions between Lebanon and its neighbors, as well as in the rise of extremist groups in the region. The bombing also had a significant impact on the US foreign policy, leading to a re-evaluation of its military presence in the region.

As the former US Secretary of State, George Shultz, noted, 'The Beirut bombing was a wake-up call for the United States, a reminder of the dangers of terrorism and the need for a more nuanced approach to foreign policy.'
